Subject: Follow-up: Feature parity & next tests  Acme

Hi Alice/Tom 

Great to meet you both earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps from today's discovery: 

Key priorities we heard
- Streaming reliability + sub-200ms token latency for live assistant flows
- Deterministic function/tool calling and structured outputs for downstream processing
- Key management (KMS/HSM) and audit logs for compliance
- Unit-cost constraints: looking for predictable per-token economics for peak 2k TPS

Proposed next tests (minimal viable evaluation):
1) Streaming test: 30-minute simulated session (10 concurrent streams) measuring tail latency and reconnect behavior (we'll stream via SSE/websocket).
2) Function calling parity: run your 100 curated tool calls (webhook+db) and validate deterministic params + error-handling window.
3) Structured output: validate JSON-schema enforcement across 500 prompts (3 schemas) and measure post-processing error rate.

Requests from our side
- Lukas (SE) will propose a concrete test matrix and runbook.
- We'll provision a short-lived dedicated instance and sample model snapshots for the tests.
- Please send any non-disclosure or SOC/infosec checklist items you want us to pre-address.

Attachments: acme-test-plan.xlsx (draft test plan), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf (high-level competitive notes)

Next steps / asks
- Lukas: can you share a 1-page test matrix and required creds by EOD tomorrow?
- Alice/Tom: confirm which week in Aug you'd like the 2-week eval window.
- Rishi: will flag procurement cadence and budget ask (cc'd).

Thanks  excited to run these with you.

Best,

Thanks Marissa  good recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Streaming: our biggest concern is tail behavior under network jitter  happy to provide a set of recorded client traces to replay. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports resume/reconnect semantics without state loss?
- Function/tool calling: we need deterministic argument ordering for idempotency during retries. Also want to validate signature verification on webhooks.
- KMS: we'll need to validate HSM-backed key wrapping for exported models and audit logs for per-request key usage. SOC2 evidence will be required for procurement.

Procurement timeline: target internal approval by end of Sep; procurement will want a 2-week pilot with cost estimate for a Dedicated pool.

I've attached the Acme infosec checklist (redacted). Can your security team provide a contact for the SOC2 artifacts?

Also looping in Tom to confirm availability for the pilot window.

On Wed, Jul 15, 2026 at 2:18 PM Alice Zhang <alice@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa  good recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
> - Streaming: our biggest concern is tail behavior under network jitter  happy to provide a set of recorded client traces to replay. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports resume/reconnect semantics without state loss?
> - Function/tool calling: we need deterministic argument ordering for idempotency during retries. Also want to validate signature verification on webhooks.
> - KMS: we'll need to validate HSM-backed key wrapping for exported models and audit logs for per-request key usage. SOC2 evidence will be required for procurement.

Hi Alice  thanks for the specifics. Quick technical notes: 
- Streaming resume: Redwood's runtime supports prefix/KV caching and session tokens for stream resumption; reconnects will replay missing tokens from a durable KV cache up to a configurable window (default 30s). We'll include a replay harness so you can replay your client traces.
- Deterministic function args: we can lock the argument serializer (stable JSON canonicalization) and provide a signed webhook verification header. We'll document the retry semantics in the runbook.
- KMS/HSM: we integrate with customer KMS via key-wrapping and can provide per-request audit logs; HSMs are supported for private deployments.

Attached is a proposed test-matrix.csv (columns: test_type, concurrency, input_set, expected_metrics) and a short runbook for the streaming harness. For the dedicated instance cost, I'll attach a baseline estimate and a note on burst capacity.

Next steps (SE):
- I'll finalize the test matrix and send a runnable harness by Fri (2026-07-17).
- Schedule a 90-minute workshop to validate traces + webhook signatures (suggest Aug 3-5).

Cheers,
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
